text:
alice-docs: opened a WIP PR to add guidance on audit export redaction levels + SDK migration examples across ruby/js and clarify SOC2 phrasing for "sealed" audit trails. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/978 (draft). Need legal wording and a short Ruby snippet for the migration guide.
carmen: can you paste the current example so i can update it?
alice-docs: current public example: `{"tenant_id": "org_555", "user_email": "lee@example.com", "event": "remove_member"}` 
car­men: (typo) 
carmen: for the docs we should stop showing raw tenant_id and user_email together. propose three export modes: none|pseudonymize|redact mapped to api param `redaction_level`. pseudonymize -> tenant_hash/user_hash; redact -> `<redacted>` tokens.
erin-ops: also call out export retention behavior. ops asks: default retention for exports is 180 days in our new policy, right? we should include `retention_days` and `retention_grace_days` meaning. auditors care about the exact defaults.
david-legal: Legal guidance: prefer precise auditor-friendly phrases. Suggest: "Audit logs and exports are persisted in an append-only, tamper-evident (sealed) audit trail. Identifiers in exports may be pseudonymized using a secret-salted HMAC-SHA256 (tenant_hash/user_hash) or irreversibly redacted. Mapping material, if retained, is access-restricted and subject to audited access controls." Also ask to mention that pseudonymization keys/salts must be stored in KMS/HSM and rotated per policy.
alice-docs: thanks, david. i'll draft paragraph and add a Ruby SDK example showing pseudonymize mode and a CLI/curl example for redact exports and deletion. any preferred wording for 'sealed'?
david-legal: 'append-only, tamper-evident (sealed) audit trail' is good. Auditors like seeing both terms. Also add sentence: 'Audit exports are encrypted at rest and in transit.'
carmen: draft paragraph added in PR: "Audit data is persisted in an append-only, tamper-evident (sealed) audit trail. When creating exports you can choose `redaction_level`: `none` (full raw fields), `pseudonymize` (replaced with tenant_hash/user_hash produced using a secret-salted HMAC-SHA256), or `redact` (irreversible redaction tokens such as `<redacted>`). Mapping material for pseudonymization is stored separately, access-restricted, and access is audited. Pseudonymization salts/keys should be stored in KMS/HSM and rotated per customer policy. Audit exports are encrypted at rest and in transit. Default export retention is 180 days; customers can override this via `export.retention_days`."
erin-ops: small request: add a one-line explanation of `retention_grace_days` (how long exports are discoverable after deletion request) so support knows what to tell customers.
carmen: added sentence about `retention_grace_days` to PR.
alice-docs: adding Ruby snippet (pseudonymize):
```ruby
# compute tenant_hash using HMAC-SHA256 with secret salt retrieved from KMS/HSM
require 'openssl'
raw = 'tenant:acme'
salt = get_salt_from_kms() # retrieve salt from KMS/HSM
h = OpenSSL::HMAC.hexdigest('sha256', salt, raw)
client.audit.log_event(tenant_hash: h, user_hash: nil, event: 'remove_member')
# do NOT include raw tenant_id or user_email in logs or exports when using pseudonymize/redact
```
david-legal: please change `get_salt_from_kms()` comment to explicit 'retrieve salt from KMS/HSM' in snippet. Also add 'audited access controls' phrase in the paragraph where you mention mapping material.
carmen: updated wording in PR per legal; added 'audited access controls' and clarified KMS/HSM. also added CLI example for redact export and delete: 
```bash
# create a redacted export via CLI
redwoodctl exports create --scope audit --redaction-level redact --retention-days 180
# delete an export (subject to retention_grace_days)
redwoodctl exports delete --export-id exp_12345
```
# and curl example for API consumers
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/exports -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"scope":"audit","redaction_level":"redact","retention_days":180}'
erin-ops: nice. also note: for `none` mode we should warn customers that raw exports contain PII and may increase compliance scope. add a short warning box in docs.
alice-docs: added warning and a short FAQ: "When to use redact vs pseudonymize?" -> redact if customer cannot or will not maintain mapping material; pseudonymize if re-linking is required for investigations but be prepared to secure mapping tables.
elink-bot: link-checker: found a broken anchor for api-reference#export-params - pushed nav fix in a follow-up commit.
build-bot: preview for PR 978: https://deploy.previews.redwood/978 build passed.
david-legal: LGTM with one tiny edit: replace 'secret-salted HMAC-SHA256' with 'secret-salted HMAC-SHA256 (e.g., HMAC-SHA256 with customer-managed salt stored in KMS/HSM)' so auditors see the explicit example.
carmen: updated per legal. CI green.
alice-docs: ready to merge if no objections. any last blockers?
erin-ops: add a changelog migration note under v2.1: 'exports now support redaction_level and default retention changed to 180 days' so customers get notified.
alice-docs: added migration changelog entry. merging now. :shipit:
david-legal: Approved. Keep conservative phrasing.
alice-docs: merged and closing thread. thanks everyone!
carmen: thanks all.
build-bot: deploy preview removed after merge.
